data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Deep learning models are trained on millions of examples; experts rely on far fewer, more varied experiences.","A checklist is an explicitly designed human artifact, while a neural network's architecture is an emergent property of optimization."],"overturn_conditions":["The non-expert panel, after training, develops a 'gestalt' sensitivity not captured by the explicit checklist.","The expert's intuition is no more reliable on edge cases than the panel's checklist-guided guesses."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a trade-off between a rigid, interpretable model (linear regression) and a flexible, opaque one (deep neural network/intuition).","Both can achieve high performance on standard cases but fail differently on out-of-distribution edge cases.","Both raise the question of whether a simpler model's success is 'genuine' understanding or mere pattern matching."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_004","SRC_006","SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The 'right answer for the wrong reasons' problem applies to both: a checklist that works by summing features may be exploiting a spurious correlation in the evaluation set, just as a linear model might.","The failure mode on edge cases is a key diagnostic: rigid systems fail predictably, flexible ones unpredictably."]},"claim":"A single domain expert relying on intuition will produce more reliable judgments, because checklists necessarily fragment high-order feature integration into discrete, linear steps, losing critical gestalt information. Within a single evaluation, genuine reliability is distinguished from mere compliance by examining the panel's behavior on novel, 'checklist-silent' edge cases: a genuinely reliable process will exhibit coherent, principled extrapolation, while mere compliance will collapse into random guessing or systematic bias when the algorithm ends.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is objectively verifiable and dominated by discrete, checkable features rather than holistic integration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition is poorly calibrated due to lack of feedback or bias.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'checklist-silent' cases are not representative of the task's core difficulty.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's 'principled extrapolation' is actually a post-hoc rationalization of a biased intuition.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition is a model of complex, non-linear feature interactions honed by feedback. A checklist is a linear approximation of this model. On tasks where success depends on a simple sum of features, the checklist panel wins. On tasks where success depends on the specific configuration or interaction of features, the linear approximation fails and the expert wins. Genuine reliability is a property of the underlying generative model. A panel showing mere compliance lacks this model and will fail when the checklist's coverage ends.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
